evidence: Crater Lake party went 'directly up from the lake to the 8,000ft col on the southeast ridge' then 'scrambling up the boulders'; summit reached through a small boulder tunnel, which the peak page rates Class 3; another report: 'only requires class 2 and low class 3'.
note: No source rates the SE ridge itself; the Class 3 crux is the shared summit block. Ridge below is Class 2-3 talus.

evidence: Peakbagger lists Rimrock Ridge (7,254 ft, parent Old Guard Peak, 1 logged ascent) with no route text; no trip report found on SummitPost, NWHikers, CascadeClimbers or blogs.
note: Searched 'Rimrock Ridge' with Glacier Peak Wilderness, Agnes Creek, Flat Creek, Sentinel Peak, Old Guard, Ptarmigan Traverse, peakbagger/listsofjohn, nwhikers/cascadeclimbers. Nothing route-specific exists online; grade is the record's own, consistent with neighbouring Old Guard's Class 3 scramble.

evidence: Only route-specific account says 'snow climb & rock scramble via Northeast Ridge' with no class; ski parties use Rock's east ridge to the Howard-Rock notch (steep, icy, ski crampons needed); Nason Ridge traverse reports call the scrambling Class 2 to Class 3.
note: No class rating exists for this line. Ski use of the ridge suggests Class 2 terrain in snow; record's Class 3 kept as the summer rock-scramble reading.

evidence: Happy Creek is 'the least demanding way up Ruby Mountain' in winter/spring; reports describe steep forested snow slopes and a final 'scramble over exposed mixed rock and snow to the summit', with a cornice to avoid on the ridge. No class number anywhere.
note: Snow route; exposed mixed summit-ridge scramble read as Class 3 (top of record's Class 2-3). Without that finish it would be Class 2.

evidence: Mountain Project lists 16 SEWS routes; none is a plain 'East Buttress'. The only east-buttress line is East Buttress Direct (Beckey-Leen 1968), 9 pitches, 5.11a or 5.9 A0, pitches 5.6/5.8/5.9+/5.11a/5.10-/5.10+/5.6/easy 5th/5.4.
note: The record's 6-pitch, 5.8-crux profile (5.6/5.7/5.8/5.7/5.6/5.4) matches no documented route; the nearest 5.8 line is the Southwest Rib (5.8, crux on pitch 1). 5.8 kept only as the record's own value.
identity: No 'East Buttress' distinct from the East Buttress Direct (5.11a / 5.9 A0, III) is documented; this row is either that route under-graded, or a misfiled other line (Southwest Rib 5.8 or South East Mank 5.7).

evidence: SummitPost route page: Rock Difficulty 5.4, Grade II, 8 pitches; 200 ft Class 4 first tower, Class 2/3, a '5th class section which involves downclimbing off of a block', then Class 3/4 to the summit; 'not a recommended route'.
note: A route database lists a Sperry 'South Ridge' alpine route at 5.2 (427 m), probably the same ridge; the route-specific page's 5.4 is preferred.

evidence: North-face snow line ('Arachnophobia') crosses a 'mammoth bergschrund' and has 'icy conditions on the final 100m of steep slope' needing ice axes; no ice grade given anywhere.
note: Steep snow with icy sections and no ice grade mapped to Class 3. Searched Kloke/Tindall/1972 in AAJ and elsewhere without finding the FA account.
identity: Ski sources call this line 'the 1976 climber's line', not 1972; the Kloke-Tindall date/party could not be confirmed online.

evidence: Treated as a winter/spring snow climb; easier line via the Pt 5261-Spinnaker col is 'steepest part of the trip' with minimal exposure, ice axe not needed; harder option over Pt 5261 follows a narrow ridge with steep drops. Summer is a brushy off-trail scramble. No class number found.
note: Easier line reads as Class 2 snow; Class 3 kept as the top of the record's Class 2-3 range covering the Pt 5261 ridge option and summer scrambling.

evidence: AAJ 1979 FA account: rappel from the Goode-Storm King saddle onto the glacier, then the '3000-foot rock rib' to the main (east) summit; roped 'leads' with runners on trees, mostly loose rock, steps kicked in snow mid-face, steep snow gully to bypass a steepening; ~12 hours. No difficulty grade given.
note: Roped leads on a rock rib with no number stated, so 5.0 per the low-5th default. The first-ascent account is signed Walter R. Gove (the record spells it 'Walt Grove'). Not the Colorado Storm King (5.7+ North Face on Mountain Project).

evidence: From Pickell Pass: 'moderate snow with some 2nd/3rd class rock at the top', 'some Class 3 rock at the top'; the SW-face line from the Fury col was soloed unroped on 'pleasantly solid' rock with no class given.
note: The record's breakdown 'Class 3-4 (low 5th possible)' for the SW face is not supported by any source found.

evidence: Trip report from the Boiling Lake side rates Switchback 'Class 2-3': 'only scrambling required was for the last 300 feet... very simple large boulders'; another report took the west gully south of the west ridge at 'class 2 climbing all the way up'.
note: Top of the Class 2-3 range; the plain west-gully line is Class 2.

evidence: Mountain Project route page: East Face, WI2 Steep Snow, 2 pitches, 200 ft; 'obvious cleft on the East Face', steep snow with 'short sections of moderate ice' in cold spells; ice axe(s) and a few screws if belayed.
note: This is Table Mountain at Heather Meadows (Mt Baker Ski Area), same face as Death Picnic (WI5).

evidence: Summer: 'Tailgunner is an easy hike up some slabby rock', an hour's add-on from Gunn; the Gunn/Tailgunner/Wing approach is Class 2 scrambling with bushwhacking. Early season a party cramponed the north slope and a relic-cornice headwall, with no class given.
note: Gunn and Wing are the Class 3 summits of this group; Tailgunner itself is not. Early-season snow can make the headwall steeper.

evidence: Route-specific trip report (Chopping Block Northwest Route): '3rd Class scramble midway up the NE Ridge, then an exposed traverse across the North face on Class 4 ledges, and an easy Class 3 scramble up the remainder of the NW Ridge'.
note: No online account of the 1961 Cooper-Denny ascent found (they made the Himmelhorn FA on 8 Sep 1961). The NE Ridge proper is a separate 5.5 route on Mountain Project.
